title: How to Use Claude Code: 2026 Beginner Guide + 18 Commands

facts.fact: Anthropic's Claude Pro plan costs $20 a month, or $17 a month billed annually ($200 a year), before tax, and includes Claude Code.
facts.quote: Pro | $20 a month, or $17 a month billed annually ($200 a year) | Included

facts.fact: Anthropic's Claude Max plan starts at $100 a month and includes Claude Code, with 5x or 20x the usage of Pro.
facts.quote: Max | From $100 a month, for 5x or 20x the usage of Pro | Included

facts.fact: Anthropic's Claude Team standard seat costs $25 a month ($20 billed annually), and the premium seat costs $125 ($100 billed annually) with 5x the usage of a standard seat.
facts.quote: Standard seat $25 a month ($20 billed annually); premium seat $125 ($100 billed annually) with 5x the usage of a standard seat

facts.fact: Anthropic's Claude Enterprise plan is listed at $20 per seat a month billed annually, plus usage at API rates.
facts.quote: Enterprise | $20 per seat a month billed annually, plus usage at API rates

facts.fact: Claude Code is not included in the Claude Free plan.
facts.quote: Pro, Max, Team and Enterprise. The Free plan does not include it

facts.fact: On older Enterprise plans, Claude Code is available only with Chat + Claude Code or Premium seats, according to the page.
facts.quote: On older Enterprise plans, Claude Code comes only with Chat + Claude Code or Premium seats.

facts.fact: On Pro and Max plans, Claude and Claude Code share the same usage limits, which include a five-hour session limit and a weekly limit.
facts.quote: a five-hour session limit and a weekly limit

facts.fact: Anthropic's native Claude Code installer for macOS, Linux and WSL is run with the curl command shown on the page.
facts.quote: Install on macOS, Linux, WSL | `curl -fsSL https://claude.ai/install.sh | bash`

facts.fact: The Windows PowerShell install command for Claude Code is irm https://claude.ai/install.ps1 | iex.
facts.quote: Install on Windows (PowerShell) | `irm https://claude.ai/install.ps1 | iex`

facts.fact: Auto permission mode is the starting mode for terminal and VS Code sessions on Claude Code v2.1.283 or later.
facts.quote: Auto mode for terminal and VS Code sessions on v2.1.283 or later. Press Shift+Tab to switch

facts.fact: The VS Code extension for Claude Code needs VS Code 1.94.0 or later.
facts.quote: It needs VS Code 1.94.0 or later.

facts.fact: Claude Code runs on macOS 13.0 or later.
facts.quote: Claude Code runs on macOS 13.0 or later, Windows 10 1809 or later

facts.fact: Claude Code runs on Windows 10 version 1809 or later, or Windows Server 2019 and later.
facts.quote: Windows 10 1809 or later (or Windows Server 2019 and later), Ubuntu 20.04+, Debian 10+ and Alpine Linux 3.19+

facts.fact: Claude Code supports Ubuntu 20.04 or later, Debian 10 or later, and Alpine Linux 3.19 or later.
facts.quote: Ubuntu 20.04+, Debian 10+ and Alpine Linux 3.19+

facts.fact: Claude Code requires at least 4 GB of RAM and an x64 or ARM64 processor.
facts.quote: You need at least 4 GB of RAM, an x64 or ARM64 processor, an internet connection

facts.fact: Press Esc twice or run /rewind in Claude Code to restore code and conversation to an earlier point.
facts.quote: Press Esc twice or run `/rewind` to restore code and conversation to an earlier point

facts.fact: The Claude Code desktop app's Code tab is available for macOS and Windows, with Linux in beta.
facts.quote: the Code tab in the Claude app for macOS and Windows, with Linux in beta

facts.fact: A Claude Console account lets users pay per use with prepaid API credits billed at standard API rates, with Claude Code available pay as you go.
facts.quote: Claude Console (API) | Prepaid API credits, billed at standard API rates | Pay as you go

facts.fact: If an ANTHROPIC_API_KEY environment variable is set and approved, the session bills that key at API rates instead of the subscription.
facts.quote: the session bills that key at API rates instead of using your subscription

facts.fact: The page states it checked Claude Code details against Anthropic's documentation, pricing page and Help Center on October 8, 2026.
facts.quote: Checked against Anthropic’s Claude Code documentation, the claude.com pricing page and the Claude Help Center on October 8, 2026.

facts.fact: Anthropic recommends installing Git for Windows on native Windows so Claude Code can use its Bash tool; without it, Claude Code uses PowerShell instead.
facts.quote: On native Windows, Anthropic recommends installing [Git for Windows](https://git-scm.com/downloads/win) so Claude Code can use its Bash tool. Without it, Claude Code uses PowerShell instead.

facts.fact: The npm installation of Claude Code requires Node.js 22 or later.
facts.quote: # npm (needs Node.js 22 or later)

facts.fact: Anthropic warns never to use sudo with npm install -g for Claude Code, because it causes permission and security problems.
facts.quote: Anthropic warns never to use `sudo npm install -g`, which causes permission and security problems.

facts.fact: Homebrew and WinGet installs of Claude Code do not update themselves and must be upgraded manually.
facts.quote: Homebrew and WinGet installs don’t update themselves, so run `brew upgrade claude-code` or `winget upgrade Anthropic.ClaudeCode` now and then.

facts.fact: Anthropic recommends keeping each CLAUDE.md file under 200 lines.
facts.quote: **Keep it short.** Aim for under 200 lines per file. Longer files use more context, and Claude follows them less reliably.

facts.fact: On current versions (v2.1.283 or later), new terminal and VS Code sessions of Claude Code start in auto permission mode.
facts.quote: On current versions (v2.1.283 or later), new terminal and VS Code sessions start in auto mode.

facts.fact: Anthropic states that auto mode in Claude Code reduces permission prompts but does not guarantee safety.
facts.quote: Anthropic is clear that auto mode reduces permission prompts but does not guarantee safety.

facts.fact: Anthropic recommends using Bypass permissions mode only in isolated environments such as containers or virtual machines.
facts.quote: Anthropic says to use it only in isolated environments such as containers or virtual machines, where Claude Code can’t cause damage.

facts.fact: In Claude Code's plan mode, Claude can read files and explore but cannot edit source code until the user approves a plan.
facts.quote: It reads files, runs commands to explore and writes a plan, but it can’t edit your source until you approve.

facts.fact: Anthropic reports an average of about $13 per developer per active day across enterprise Claude Code deployments.
facts.unit: USD per developer per active day
facts.quote: Anthropic reports an average of about $13 per developer per active day across enterprise deployments, or $150 to $250 per developer per month

facts.fact: Anthropic reports that across enterprise Claude Code deployments, 150 to 250 USD per developer per month is typical.
facts.quote: or $150 to $250 per developer per month, with 90% of users under $30 per active day

facts.fact: Anthropic reports that 90% of Claude Code enterprise users spend under 30 USD per active day.
facts.unit: % of users under $30 per active day
facts.quote: with 90% of users under $30 per active day

facts.fact: The article states that the --max-budget-usd flag caps how much a single scripted claude -p run can spend.
facts.quote: the `--max-budget-usd` flag caps what a single run can spend

facts.fact: On Free, Pro and Max plans, Anthropic trains on Claude Code session data only when the user's model-improvement setting is on.
facts.quote: On Free, Pro and Max, Anthropic trains on your data, including Claude Code sessions, only when your model-improvement setting is on

facts.fact: On Team, Enterprise and API plans, Anthropic does not train on code or prompts sent to Claude Code unless the organization opts in.
facts.quote: On Team, Enterprise and the API, Anthropic doesn’t train on code or prompts sent to Claude Code unless your organization opts in.

facts.fact: Claude Code's deny rules take precedence over allow rules in permission settings.
facts.quote: Deny rules win over allow rules.

facts.fact: Rewind restores Claude's file edits but does not track changes made by shell commands such as rm, mv or cp.
facts.quote: Rewind restores Claude’s file edits, but it doesn’t track changes made by shell commands such as rm, mv or cp

facts.fact: The /usage command shows plan limits on Pro, Max, Team and Enterprise plans.
facts.quote: On Pro, Max, Team and Enterprise it shows your plan limits and what is using them

facts.fact: Anthropic's docs say Sonnet handles most coding tasks well and costs less than Opus.
facts.quote: Anthropic’s docs say Sonnet handles most coding tasks well and costs less than Opus.

facts.fact: Claude Code permission rules are enforced by Claude Code itself rather than by the model.
facts.quote: Permission rules are enforced by Claude Code itself, not by the model, so they hold even if Claude misreads an instruction.

facts.fact: Anthropic's best-practices guide calls verification the biggest lever for getting good results from Claude Code.
facts.quote: Anthropic’s best-practices guide calls verification the biggest lever

facts.fact: Claude Code is not included in the free Claude plan; a paid Pro, Max, Team or Enterprise plan is needed, or a Claude Console account billed per use at API rates.
facts.quote: No, Claude Code isn't included in the free Claude plan. You need a Pro, Max, Team or Enterprise plan (Pro is $20 a month)

facts.fact: The Claude Pro plan costs $20 a month, or $17 a month when billed annually, per the page.
facts.quote: Pro is the cheapest way in at $20 a month, or $17 a month billed annually.

facts.fact: The Claude Max plan starts at $100 a month, offering 5x or 20x the Pro usage.
facts.quote: Max starts at $100 a month for 5x or 20x the Pro usage

facts.fact: On Pro and Max plans, Claude and Claude Code share the same five-hour session limit and weekly limit.
facts.quote: On Pro and Max, Claude and Claude Code share the same five-hour session limit and weekly limit.

facts.quote: it needs VS Code 1.94.0 or later and also works in Cursor

facts.fact: Anthropic suggests clearing the session and writing a better first prompt after two failed corrections in Claude Code.
facts.quote: After two failed corrections, Anthropic suggests clearing and writing a better first prompt.

facts.fact: CLAUDE.md files should be kept under about 200 lines, according to the page's guidance.
facts.quote: Run /init to generate one, keep it under about 200 lines, and edit it with /memory.
